atoms.text: This guide describes the bucket policy statement that lets the Quarry interactive query engine store query results in the bucket acme-quarry-results. Quarry runs SQL against tables defined over data in other buckets and writes each result set as a compressed CSV file under the results/ prefix. The statement allows s3:PutObject, s3:AbortMultipartUpload and s3:ListMultipartUploadParts on arn:aws:s3:::acme-quarry-results/results/*, plus s3:GetBucketLocation and s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN. In the Principal element, name the IAM role that the workgroup assumes for query execution, for example arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/QuarryQueryExecutionRole. Because the role is in the same account as the bucket, either this policy or the role's identity-based policy could grant access, but keeping the grant in the bucket policy makes it easier to audit. Add a separate Deny statement for requests where aws:SecureTransport is false. To verify the setup, run a query in the workgroup and confirm that an object named after the query ID appears under results/. If the query fails with Access Denied during output, check that the role ARN in the Principal element matches the role attached to the workgroup.

This guide describes the bucket policy statement that lets the Quarry interactive query engine store query results in the bucket acme-quarry-results. Quarry runs SQL against tables defined over data in other buckets and writes each result set as a compressed CSV file under the results/ prefix. The statement allows s3:PutObject, s3:AbortMultipartUpload and s3:ListMultipartUploadParts on arn:aws:s3:::acme-quarry-results/results/*, plus s3:GetBucketLocation and s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN. In the Principal element, name the service principal quarry.amazonaws.com instead of any role or account. Restrict it with an aws:SourceAccount condition set to 111122223333 and an aws:SourceArn condition set to arn:aws:quarry:us-east-1:111122223333:workgroup/*, so that only workgroups in your account can use the grant. Add a separate Deny statement for requests where aws:SecureTransport is false. To verify the setup, run a query in the workgroup and confirm that an object named after the query ID appears under results/. If the query fails with Access Denied during output, check that the source ARN pattern covers the Region and workgroup that issued the request.

This guide covers the bucket policy statement for the Forgeflow batch transformation service, which reads raw input files and writes transformed output in the bucket acme-ingest-landing. Forgeflow jobs read newline-delimited JSON files from the raw/ prefix and write Parquet files to the curated/ prefix of the same bucket. The statement grants s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-ingest-landing/raw/*, s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-ingest-landing/curated/*, and s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN with an s3:prefix condition limited to raw/ and curated/. The Principal element names the IAM role attached to the job definition, such as arn:aws:iam::222233334444:role/ForgeflowJobRole. Each job run uses this role's credentials, so changing the job's role requires updating the Principal ARN. Do not grant s3:DeleteObject, because Forgeflow overwrites output files by key and does not need to remove input. After applying the policy, start a test job against a small sample file and check that a Parquet file appears under curated/. A 403 on the first read usually means the job is running under a different role than the one listed.

This guide covers the bucket policy statement for the Forgeflow batch transformation service, which reads raw input files and writes transformed output in the bucket acme-ingest-landing. Forgeflow jobs read newline-delimited JSON files from the raw/ prefix and write Parquet files to the curated/ prefix of the same bucket. The statement grants s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-ingest-landing/raw/*, s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-ingest-landing/curated/*, and s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN with an s3:prefix condition limited to raw/ and curated/. The Principal element names the service principal forgeflow.amazonaws.com. Add aws:SourceAccount set to 222233334444 and aws:SourceArn set to arn:aws:forgeflow:eu-west-1:222233334444:job/* so the grant applies only to jobs in your account. Do not grant s3:DeleteObject, because Forgeflow overwrites output files by key and does not need to remove input. After applying the policy, start a test job against a small sample file and check that a Parquet file appears under curated/. A 403 on the first read usually means the job ARN does not match the source ARN condition.

This guide explains the bucket policy statement for the Logsight log analytics service, which reads archived application logs and writes aggregated anomaly reports in the bucket acme-app-logs. Logsight scans gzip-compressed JSON log files under the archive/ prefix on a schedule. After each scan it writes a summary report as a JSON object under the reports/ prefix. The statement allows s3:GetObject on the archive/ objects, s3:PutObject on the reports/ objects, and s3:ListBucket on the bucket with a prefix condition for archive/. The Principal is the IAM user or role used by the analysis pipeline, for example arn:aws:iam::333344445555:user/logsight-analysis. If you use an IAM user, rotate its access keys on a fixed schedule because the scans depend on long-lived credentials. Require the s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption header to equal AES256 on writes to reports/. Verify by triggering a manual scan and confirming that a report object is created with encryption metadata. Failed scans that log AccessDenied on ListBucket typically indicate a missing prefix in the condition.

This guide explains the bucket policy statement for the Logsight log analytics service, which reads archived application logs and writes aggregated anomaly reports in the bucket acme-app-logs. Logsight scans gzip-compressed JSON log files under the archive/ prefix on a schedule. After each scan it writes a summary report as a JSON object under the reports/ prefix. The statement allows s3:GetObject on the archive/ objects, s3:PutObject on the reports/ objects, and s3:ListBucket on the bucket with a prefix condition for archive/. The Principal is the service principal logsight.amazonaws.com, limited by aws:SourceAccount set to 333344445555 and aws:SourceArn set to arn:aws:logsight:us-west-2:333344445555:analyzer/*. Because the service uses its own identity, no access keys or role credentials need to be rotated for this grant. Require the s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption header to equal AES256 on writes to reports/. Verify by triggering a manual scan and confirming that a report object is created with encryption metadata. Failed scans that log AccessDenied on ListBucket typically indicate a missing prefix in the condition.

This guide describes the bucket policy statement used by the Streamweave stream aggregation service to persist windowed rollups in the bucket acme-stream-rollups. Streamweave consumes events from an upstream stream and writes one-minute aggregates as Avro files under the rollups/ prefix. It also writes and reads checkpoint files under the checkpoints/ prefix so that a restarted application can resume from its last committed offset. The statement grants s3:PutObject and s3:GetObject on both prefixes and s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN. In the Principal element, specify the IAM role assumed by the aggregation application, such as arn:aws:iam::444455556666:role/StreamweaveAppRole. Deny any principal other than this role from writing under checkpoints/, so that checkpoints cannot be modified by other identities. After deployment, run the application for several minutes and confirm that new rollup files appear at one-minute intervals. If the application restarts with no prior state, verify that its role can read the checkpoint objects.

Streamweave consumes events from an upstream stream and writes one-minute aggregates as Avro files under the rollups/ prefix. The statement grants s3:PutObject and s3:GetObject on both prefixes and s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN. In the Principal element, specify the service principal streamweave.amazonaws.com, with aws:SourceAccount set to 444455556666 and aws:SourceArn set to arn:aws:streamweave:us-east-2:444455556666:application/*. Deny any principal other than this service principal from writing under checkpoints/, so that checkpoints cannot be modified by other identities. After deployment, run the application for several minutes and confirm that new rollup files appear at one-minute intervals. If the application restarts with no prior state, verify that the source ARN condition matches the application that wrote the checkpoint.

This guide describes a bucket policy statement for a cross-account data lake, where the bucket acme-lake-curated belongs to a producer account and is read by an analytics team in another account. The Parquet datasets under the sales/ prefix are read by Tablemill, a distributed query service, and its job output is written back to the results/ prefix of the same bucket. The statement grants s3:GetObject on sales/*, s3:PutObject on results/*, and s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN. The Principal names the consumer account, for example arn:aws:iam::555566667777:root, which delegates the decision on which identities may use the grant to that account's administrators. Those administrators must attach an identity-based policy to the Tablemill execution role that allows the same actions on this bucket. Without that second policy, the cross-account request is denied even though the bucket policy permits it. To test, run a small Tablemill job from the consumer account and check that output appears under results/. Review the list of roles in the consumer account periodically, since any role granted access there can use this statement.

This guide describes a bucket policy statement for a cross-account data lake, where the bucket acme-lake-curated belongs to a producer account and is read by an analytics team in another account. The Parquet datasets under the sales/ prefix are read by Tablemill, a distributed query service, and its job output is written back to the results/ prefix of the same bucket. The statement grants s3:GetObject on sales/*, s3:PutObject on results/*, and s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN. The Principal names the service principal tablemill.amazonaws.com, with aws:SourceAccount set to the consumer account 555566667777 and aws:SourceArn set to arn:aws:tablemill:us-east-1:555566667777:cluster/*. The service calls the bucket using its own identity, so no role in the consumer account needs a matching identity-based policy for this bucket. Requests that arrive from other accounts are rejected by the source conditions even though the service principal is shared by all customers. To test, run a small Tablemill job from the consumer account and check that output appears under results/. Review the source ARN pattern periodically, since any cluster in that account can use this statement.

This guide documents the bucket policy statement for the Featurist feature engineering service, which reads training data and writes feature snapshots in the bucket acme-ml-features. Featurist jobs read date-partitioned Parquet files under the training/ prefix and write computed feature tables underthe snapshots/ prefix. The statement allows s3:GetObject on training/*, s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload on snapshots/*, and s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN. In the Principal element, list the IAM role created for the feature jobs, for example arn:aws:iam::666677778888:role/FeaturistJobRole. Include an aws:PrincipalTag condition requiring the tag team to equal data-science, so that only role sessions carrying that tag can use the grant. Large snapshot files are uploaded in multiple parts, so the abort permission is needed to clean up incomplete uploads. Validate the configuration by running a job on one day's partition and confirming that a snapshot file is created. An AccessDenied error on read often means the role session is missing the required tag.

This guide documents the bucket policy statement for the Featurist feature engineering service, which reads training data and writes feature snapshots in the bucket acme-ml-features. Featurist jobs read date-partitioned Parquet files under the training/ prefix and write computed feature tables under the snapshots/ prefix. The statement allows s3:GetObject on training/*, s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload on snapshots/*, and s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN. In the Principal element, list the service principal featurist.amazonaws.com. Include an aws:SourceArn condition set to arn:aws:featurist:us-east-1:666677778888:job/team-data-science-*, so that only jobs following the team naming convention in that account can use the grant. Large snapshot files are uploaded in multiple parts, so the abort permission is needed to clean up incomplete uploads. Validate the configuration by running a job on one day's partition and confirming that a snapshot file is created. An AccessDenied error on read often means the job name does not match the source ARN pattern.

This guide shows the bucket policy statement for the Reportly scheduled export service, which reads dataset snapshots and writes recurring report files to the bucket acme-report-exports. Each Monday, Reportly reads the snapshot files under the snapshots/weekly/ prefix and writes a CSV export to the exports/ prefix with the report date in the key name. The statement allows s3:GetObject on snapshots/weekly/*, s3:PutObject on exports/*, and s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN restricted to those two prefixes. The Principal names the IAM role that the schedule uses to run exports, such as arn:aws:iam::777788889999:role/ReportlyScheduleRole. Because exports run unattended, set a bucket lifecycle rule that expires objects under exports/ after 90 days. Do not grant s3:PutObjectAcl, since the exported objects inherit the bucket owner's ownership settings. After saving the policy, run the schedule once on demand and check that a dated CSV file is created. If the run fails, confirm that the schedule is configured to assume the role named in the Principal element.

This guide shows the bucket policy statement for the Reportly scheduled export service, which reads dataset snapshots and writes recurring report files to the bucket acme-report-exports. Each Monday, Reportly reads the snapshot files under the snapshots/weekly/ prefix and writes a CSV export to the exports/ prefix with the report date in the key name. The statement allows s3:GetObject on snapshots/weekly/*, s3:PutObject on exports/*, and s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN restricted to those two prefixes. The Principal names the service principal reportly.amazonaws.com, with aws:SourceAccount set to 777788889999 and aws:SourceArn set to arn:aws:reportly:us-east-1:777788889999:schedule/*. Because exports run unattended, set a bucket lifecycle rule that expires objects under exports/ after 90 days. Do not grant s3:PutObjectAcl, since the exported objects inherit the bucket owner's ownership settings. After saving the policy, run the schedule once on demand and check that a dated CSV file is created. If the run fails, confirm that the schedule's ARN falls within the source ARN pattern.

This guide describes the bucket policy statement for the Datascope data profiling service, which reads input files and writes profile reports in the bucket acme-profiling. Datascope samples files under the datasets/ prefix to compute column statistics and null counts. It writes one JSON profile report per dataset under the profiles/ prefix. The statement grants s3:GetObject on datasets/*, s3:PutObject on profiles/*, and s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN. In the Principal element, specify the IAM role that the profiling jobs run under, for example arn:aws:iam::888899990000:role/DatascopeProfilerRole. Add a condition requiring s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption to equal aws:kms on writes to profiles/, and make sure the role also has permission to use the referenced KMS key. Reports that omit the encryption header are rejected, which is the intended behavior. Validate by profiling one dataset and reading back the report object. A PutObject failure with AccessDenied commonly means the job's write request lacks the encryption header or the role lacks the key permission.

This guide describes the bucket policy statement for the Datascope data profiling service, which reads input files and writes profile reports in the bucket acme-profiling. Datascope samples files under the datasets/ prefix to compute column statistics and null counts. It writes one JSON profile report per dataset under the profiles/ prefix. The statement grants s3:GetObject on datasets/*, s3:PutObject on profiles/*, and s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN. In the Principal element, specify the service principal datascope.amazonaws.com, with aws:SourceAccount set to 888899990000 and aws:SourceArn set to arn:aws:datascope:ap-southeast-2:888899990000:profiler/*. Add a condition requiring s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption to equal aws:kms on writes to profiles/, and make sure the KMS key policy also allows the service to use that key. Reports that omit the encryption header are rejected, which is the intended behavior. Validate by profiling one dataset and reading back the report object. A PutObject failure with AccessDenied commonly means the write request lacks the encryption header or the key policy does not permit the service.
